extracted.intended_audience: readers and aspiring periodical essayists/columnists (early-18th-century London audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Crafting short moral and social periodical essays that combine plain narrative, observation, anecdote, and ethical reflection for a general literate public. Emphasizes natural style, relevance to readers, and restraint in satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness and ease (avoid frothy 'wit')
rubrics_metrics.description: What, I pray, is Natural? That which is pleasing and easie: And what are Pleasing and Easie? Forsooth, a new Thought or Conceit dressed up in smooth quaint Language, to make you smile and wag your Head, as being what you never imagined before, and yet wonder why you had not; meer frothy Amusements!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer natural, pleasing, and easy expression over elaborate conceits and ornamental 'wit'. Anti-pattern: writing that is merely 'frothy Amusements'—clever turns with little substance that please superficially (fit only for Boys or silly Women, per the essay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain narrative grounded in personal experience
rubrics_metrics.description: I, a Tradesman, shall give you another Account of this Matter in the plain Narrative of my own Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete personal anecdotes and profitable observation rather than abstract speculation. The essayist values sound judgment and observable facts over speculative invention; employ plain narrative to illustrate points rather than philosophical abstraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid defamatory libel and scurrility in satire
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing so scandalous to a Government, and detestable in the Eyes of all good Men, as defamatory Papers and Pamphlets... Our Satyr is nothing but Ribaldry, and Billingsgate. Scurrility passes for Wit; and he who can call Names in the greatest Variety of Phrases, is looked upon to have the shrewdest Pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire should not pursue private defamation or gratuitous scurrility. Targeting individuals' reputations is morally wrong and socially harmful; excellent satire accepts limits of humanity and truth. Historical/legal consequences are cited as supporting restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity has value; forced author identification can stifle learning
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been proposed, to oblige every Person that writes a Book, or a Paper, to swear himself the Author of it, and enter down in a publick Register his Name and Place of Abode... such an Expedient would not only destroy Scandal, but Learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that anonymous or pseudonymous publication can encourage experiment and the emergence of works of genius; a policy forcing disclosure may root up both scandal and valuable anonymous contributions. Consider anonymity as a legitimate publishing practice for early-stage or delicate works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readers and disseminators of libel share culpability
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot imagine, that a Man who disperses a Libel is less desirous of doing Mischief than the Author himself... I shall here add the Words of a Modern Author... 'I cannot imagine, that a Man who disperses a Libel is less desirous of doing Mischief than the Author himself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that enjoyment or distribution of defamatory material implicates the reader/distributor ethically; writers should avoid producing such material, and readers/editors should avoid amplifying it.

rubrics_metrics.name: News-writing: favour depth and relevance over mere novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Humour in my Countrymen, which I am more inclined to wonder at, than their general Thirst after News... They are Men of a Voracious Appetite, but no Taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid serving up novelty for novelty's sake. Prefer material that has lasting interest (history, travels) or real relevance to the intended readership. Anti-pattern: filling copy with trivial 'boat-news' or sensational scraps that satisfy curiosity only momentarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide commentary and context, not just raw intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Text is given us by one set of writers, and the Comment by another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News or intelligence benefits from interpretive commentary. Editors/essayists should not only transmit facts but also supply observations, reflections, and explanations that make the facts meaningful to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose elevated, imagination-inspiring subjects for serious poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: If Gratitude is due from Man to Man, how much more from Man to his Maker?... our Idea of the Supream Being is... filled with every thing that can raise the Imagination, and give an Opportunity for the sublimest Thoughts and Conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For devotional or serious verse, select subjects (e.g., gratitude toward the divine) that naturally lift the imagination and suit lofty treatment. Avoid treating exalted subjects with triviality or moral absurdity as in pagan examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express sincere emotional tone in devotional/moral pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: There is not a more pleasing Exercise of the Mind than Gratitude. It is accompanied with such an inward Satisfaction, that the Duty is sufficiently rewarded by the Performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In moral or devotional writing aim for genuine warmth and inward satisfaction rather than forced fervour. The tone should feel naturally pleasurable rather than painful or ostentatious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid, concrete sensory detail and social types for observational prose
rubrics_metrics.description: It was the most pleasing Scene imaginable to see the Chearfulness with which those industrious People ply'd their Way... I strolled from one Fruit-Shop to another, with Crowds of agreeable young Women around me... I saw immediately she was of the Family of the Vainloves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground essays in specific scenes, occupations, gestures, and market-detail to animate writing. Character-types can be sketched economically by recurring habitual behaviors and concrete signs rather than explicit labels alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support general claims with concrete episodes and quantified particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Year 1665, when the Sickness was, I lost by it my Wife and two Children... with about £2000 and a little Credit, I bought as much Tobacco as rais'd my Estate to the Value of £10000... I recovered 15000 Pounds... put a Silence to all my Neighbours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When arguing about social effects or moral consequences, supply illustrative incidents, chronological narrative, and even specific sums or counts to make the claim persuasive. Numbers and particulars help demonstrate experience-based authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a moderate, non-partisan moral voice
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot think that any one will be so unjust as to imagine, what I have here said is spoken with a Respect to any Party or Faction... Every one who has in him the Sentiments either of a Christian or a Gentleman, cannot but be highly offended at this wicked and ungenerous Practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid partisan invective; moral criticism should be presented as general and principled rather than as factional attack. Keep the voice measured and appeal to shared civic/religious values to persuade a broad readership.
